hardestQuestions.text: A directed network has five labeled vertices, with fixed distinct source s and sink t. How many vertex partitions satisfy s in S and t in T before any cut capacities are evaluated?
hardestQuestions.topic: Minimum s-t Cut Principle & Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem

hardestQuestions.text: For a chain of three matrices with dimension sequence p = [5, 10, 3, 12], choose the minimum total scalar-multiplication count over both legal parenthesizations.
The complete matrix-chain input is n = 1 and p = [7, 11]. The judged output is the minimum scalar-multiplication count. What integer should the program print?
A chain has dimensions p = [1, 10, 1, 10, 1]. Preserving the matrix order, what minimum scalar-multiplication count can interval DP achieve?
An Edmonds-Karp BFS has found the sink, and its parent records reconstruct a path whose residual capacities are 8, 3, and 5. Which reduction over these capacities gives the augmentation amount?
Ten units of selected value are moved from an item of density 2 to available value from an item of density 5. By how much does selected weight decrease?
All item weights and values are positive and fractions are unrestricted in [0,1]. For a feasible positive target P, what can be said about the selected value in every minimum-weight solution?
options: It can be less than P if the weight is smaller
It must strictly exceed P whenever a fractional item is used
It must equal the sum of all item values

hardestQuestions.text: Several discovered cells can share an eligible neighbor. What invariant is obtained by marking that neighbor when it is pushed rather than waiting until it is popped?
options: The stack always contains cells in shortest-path order
Every eligible cell is pushed at most once
Every grid cell must be pushed even if its color differs
The DFS uses only constant memory for every image
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: Every eligible cell is pushed at most once

hardestQuestions.text: A bottom-up matrix-chain algorithm must ensure that both subchains of a candidate split are already solved. Which outer processing order guarantees this property?
options: Process intervals in decreasing number of matrices
Process split indices in random order before any states
Process intervals in increasing number of matrices
Process only the main diagonal and the final interval
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: Process intervals in increasing number of matrices

hardestQuestions.text: A chain contains five matrices, each of size 3 by 3. Using standard multiplication, what minimum scalar-multiplication count is obtained for their product?
What is a after exactly four iterations of this complete C++17 local computation? long long a=0,b=1; for(int i=0;i<4;++i){long long next=a+b; a=b; b=next;}
A valid minimum-cut input has N=5, M=0, source 2, and sink 5. What happens when Edmonds-Karp performs its first source-to-sink BFS?
options: The source automatically becomes the sink because M is zero
The sink is unreachable, so the total flow remains zero
The algorithm must return a negative cut capacity
The algorithm must invent a direct source-to-sink edge
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: The sink is unreachable, so the total flow remains zero
hardestQuestions.topic: Minimum s-t Cut Principle & Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem

hardestQuestions.text: Four matrices A1, A2, A3, and A4 must retain their order. How many distinct full binary parenthesizations exist before comparing their scalar-multiplication costs?
After a network header N M s t, each edge line has the format u v c. In this format, what does the edge line 2 4 7 describe?
options: A directed edge from vertex 4 to vertex 2 with capacity 7
Seven parallel edges from vertex 2 to vertex 4, each with unspecified capacity
A required flow of 4 from vertex 2 to vertex 7
A directed edge from vertex 2 to vertex 4 with capacity 7
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: A directed edge from vertex 2 to vertex 4 with capacity 7

hardestQuestions.text: Under a unit-cost arithmetic model, Edmonds-Karp has the standard bound O(V*E^2). If V and E stay fixed while integer capacities become numerically larger, what does that bound say about the augmentation count?
options: It must enumerate every integer from zero to the largest capacity
Its standard graph-size bound does not grow in proportion to the maximum flow value
It becomes an exhaustive search over all assignments of edge flows
It must perform exactly one augmentation for each unit of maximum flow
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: Its standard graph-size bound does not grow in proportion to the maximum flow value

hardestQuestions.text: A Fibonacci program must avoid recursion while still storing all Fi values from index 0 through n. Which implementation most directly meets that requirement?
options: Initialize base cases and fill a table iteratively from smaller indices to larger ones
Sort the indices by their Fibonacci values before computing any state
Use two uncached recursive calls for every non-base index
Compute only Fn recursively and discard all earlier values
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: Initialize base cases and fill a table iteratively from smaller indices to larger ones

hardestQuestions.text: An Edmonds-Karp BFS from source s can no longer reach sink t through positive-residual edges. What should the maximum-flow phase do at that point?
options: Restart from zero flow and ignore reverse edges
Increase every original capacity by one
Stop, because there is no augmenting path
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: Stop, because there is no augmenting path

hardestQuestions.text: For flower prices a >= b and multipliers p <= q, which pairing has minimum cost?
options: a with p and b with q
Both flowers with q regardless of buyer counts
a with q and b with p
hardestQuestions.correctAnswer: a with p and b with q

wrongQuestions.assignmentTitle: Assignment 6 - Graph Traversal & Minimum Spanning Trees
wrongQuestions.questionText: A simple cycle graph has all edges with identical weight. How are its edges classified?
options: All are pseudo-critical and none is critical
No edge can appear in an MST
wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: All are pseudo-critical and none is critical
wrongQuestions.rule: A graph G = (V, E) connects vertices with edges. In undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional; handshaking lemma states sum(deg(v)) = 2E.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Assuming complete graph has V edges (a complete graph has V*(V-1)/2 edges).
wrongQuestions.tip: Know edge counts: trees have V-1 edges, complete graphs have O(V^2) edges.

wrongQuestions.assignmentTitle: Assignment 6 - Graph Traversal & Minimum Spanning Trees
wrongQuestions.questionText: Why does ordinary BFS fail to guarantee minimum total cost when edge weights differ?
options: It minimizes edge count, not arbitrary summed weights
wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: It minimizes edge count, not arbitrary summed weights
wrongQuestions.rule: BFS explores vertices level-by-level using a FIFO Queue. In unweighted graphs, BFS guarantees finding shortest paths in fewest edges.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Failing to mark vertices visited upon enqueue, resulting in redundant processing and memory explosion.
wrongQuestions.tip: BFS time complexity is O(V + E). Perfect for maze routing and unweighted reachability.

wrongQuestions.assignmentTitle: Assignment 6 - Graph Traversal & Minimum Spanning Trees

wrongQuestions.assignmentTitle: Assignment 6 - Graph Traversal & Minimum Spanning Trees
wrongQuestions.questionText: Prim starts at A in a graph with AB=1, AC=4, BC=2. Which edge is chosen first?
wrongQuestions.rule: Grows a single connected tree from an arbitrary starting vertex by always picking the cheapest crossing edge to an unvisited vertex using a min-heap.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Confusing Prim's single-tree growth with Kruskal's forest-merging approach.
wrongQuestions.tip: Prim with min-heap runs in O((V + E) log V); best suited for dense graphs (E ~ V^2).

wrongQuestions.assignmentTitle: Assignment 6 - Graph Traversal & Minimum Spanning Trees
wrongQuestions.questionText: In a connected graph with a unique MST, an edge not in that MST is:
wrongQuestions.rule: Cut Property: For any partition of V into (S, V - S), the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to some MST. If weights are distinct, MST is unique.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Confusing MST (minimizes sum of all edge weights) with shortest path tree (minimizes distance from a single source).
wrongQuestions.tip: A spanning tree on V vertices always contains exactly V - 1 edges and no cycles.

assignments.title: Assignment 7 - Heaps & Priority Queues

wrongQuestions.questionText: In a max-heap, each parent is:
options: At least as large as its children
At most as large as its children
wrongQuestions.selectedOption: At most as large as its children
wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: At least as large as its children
wrongQuestions.rule: A binary heap is a complete binary tree where all levels except possibly the last are fully filled from left to right.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Assuming heaps are fully sorted (left child is NOT guaranteed to be smaller/larger than right child).
wrongQuestions.tip: Max-heap: root is absolute maximum. Min-heap: root is absolute minimum.

assignments.recommendation: Proficient! 87.5% accuracy. Quick review of minor edge cases recommended.

assignments.title: Assignment 8 - Greedy Algorithms

wrongQuestions.questionText: For array [-3, 0, 2, 7], what is the minimum absolute difference between values at two distinct positions?
wrongQuestions.rule: Sort the array in O(N log N). The minimum difference between any two elements is guaranteed to occur between adjacent elements.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Comparing all pairs in O(N^2) time or comparing only maximum and minimum.
wrongQuestions.tip: Sort first, then do a single linear scan checking A[i+1] - A[i].

assignments.recommendation: Proficient! 88.9% accuracy. Quick review of minor edge cases recommended.

wrongQuestions.questionText: Does changing item order change the optimum of correctly implemented 0/1 knapsack?
options: No; because every item is selected
Yes; sorting by weight changes values
Yes; the first item must always be selected
No; the feasible subsets and their values remain the same
wrongQuestions.selectedOption: Yes; sorting by weight changes values
wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: No; the feasible subsets and their values remain the same
wrongQuestions.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
wrongQuestions.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

wrongQuestions.questionText: Double-ended Strings: a = "ababa", b = "babab". What is the minimum number of endpoint deletions to make them equal?
wrongQuestions.rule: Minimum endpoint deletions to make two strings identical equals (len(s1) + len(s2) - 2 * LCS(s1, s2)).
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Trying arbitrary character removals without recognizing that preserved characters form the LCS.
wrongQuestions.tip: Reducing string edit problems to LCS often yields straightforward DP solutions.

assignments.title: Assignment 10 - Revision Assignment

wrongQuestions.questionText: After a DP table F[0..n] has been computed under the assignment's state definition, which expression gives the answer without charging another step?
wrongQuestions.rule: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Base cases: start at step 0 or 1 with zero prior cost.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Forgetting to take min of the final two steps to reach the top floor: min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).
wrongQuestions.tip: Can be solved in O(1) auxiliary space using two variables prev1 and prev2.

wrongQuestions.questionText: When an undirected road (u,v,w) is loaded into a Floyd-Warshall matrix, what initialization preserves the road's meaning?
options: Set only dist[u][v] to w and leave dist[v][u] infinite
Set dist[u][u] and dist[v][v] to w instead
Set both dist[u][v] and dist[v][u] to w
wrongQuestions.selectedOption: Set only dist[u][v] to w and leave dist[v][u] infinite
wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: Set both dist[u][v] and dist[v][u] to w
wrongQuestions.rule: All-pairs shortest path: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]). Intermediate vertex k loop MUST be outermost.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Placing intermediate vertex k loop inside the i, j loops, breaking DP intermediate-state invariants.
wrongQuestions.tip: Runs in O(V^3) time. Finds city with smallest number of reachable neighbors within threshold.

wrongQuestions.questionText: All item weights and values are positive and fractions are unrestricted in [0,1]. For a feasible positive target P, what can be said about the selected value in every minimum-weight solution?
options: It can be less than P if the weight is smaller
It must strictly exceed P whenever a fractional item is used
It must equal the sum of all item values
wrongQuestions.selectedOption: It must strictly exceed P whenever a fractional item is used
wrongQuestions.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
wrongQuestions.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

wrongQuestions.questionText: There are six staircase steps, each costing 7. With the assignment's starting and movement rules, what is the minimum cost?
wrongQuestions.rule: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Base cases: start at step 0 or 1 with zero prior cost.
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Forgetting to take min of the final two steps to reach the top floor: min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).
wrongQuestions.tip: Can be solved in O(1) auxiliary space using two variables prev1 and prev2.

wrongQuestions.questionText: What is the assignment's unit-cost edit distance from 'kitten' to 'sitting'?
wrongQuestions.rule: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1]; else 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).
wrongQuestions.pitfall: Adding cost +1 when characters match; matching characters cost 0 edits.
wrongQuestions.tip: Base cases: dp[i][0] = i (deleting i chars), dp[0][j] = j (inserting j chars).

wrongQuestions.questionText: In C++17, p is an int array and p[a] = p[b] = p[c] = 10000. Which expression safely computes their product before assigning it to a long long matrix-chain cost?
wrongQuestions.rule: m[i][j] = min_{i<=k<j} (m[i][k] + m[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j]). Base case m[i][i] = 0.

wrongQuestions.questionText: The Fibonacci assignment asks a program to print every term F0 through Fn. If each printed integer costs one time unit, what is the tight growth rate of the time spent only on these output operations?
wrongQuestions.rule: F[n] = F[n-1] + F[n-2] with F[0]=0, F[1]=1. Compute iteratively in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

wrongQuestions.correctAnswer: Both operands already have type long long

wrongQuestions.questionText: A network has N=4, source 1, sink 4, and only edges 1->2(3), 2->4(2), 1->3(4), 3->4(3), with capacities in parentheses. What minimum cut capacity should be printed?
wrongQuestions.rule: Forward residual capacity c_f(u, v) = c(u, v) - f(u, v). Backward residual capacity c_f(v, u) = f(u, v) enables flow cancellation.

wrongQuestions.tip: Residual network allows searching for augmentations even after initial flows are pushed.

topics.tip: Simulate priority-based games by pairing a max-heap with loop termination when heap size <= 1.

topics.rule: Cut Property: For any partition of V into (S, V - S), the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to some MST. If weights are distinct, MST is unique.
topics.pitfall: Confusing MST (minimizes sum of all edge weights) with shortest path tree (minimizes distance from a single source).
topics.tip: A spanning tree on V vertices always contains exactly V - 1 edges and no cycles.

topics.rule: Edmonds-Karp finds augmenting paths using BFS (shortest path in edge count). Runs in O(V * E^2) time.
topics.pitfall: Using DFS (Ford-Fulkerson) which can take O(E * max_flow) exponential time with bad path choices.
topics.tip: BFS guarantees augmenting path length never decreases, bounding total augmentations to O(V * E).

topics.rule: Forward residual capacity c_f(u, v) = c(u, v) - f(u, v). Backward residual capacity c_f(v, u) = f(u, v) enables flow cancellation.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to add backward edge with capacity equal to sent flow, preventing cancellation of suboptimal earlier decisions.
topics.tip: Residual network allows searching for augmentations even after initial flows are pushed.

topics.rule: Find two nodes summing to target. Either maintain a HashSet of visited values during traversal O(N), or use two-pointer forward and reverse in-order iterators in O(H) space.
topics.pitfall: Brute force quadratic search O(N^2) instead of leveraging BST ordered structure or hashing.
topics.tip: Two-pointer on sorted in-order traversal gives optimal O(N) time and O(H) auxiliary stack space.

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.topic: Minimum s-t Cut Principle & Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
topics.rule: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem: Maximum flow through network equals minimum capacity among all cuts separating source s and sink t.
topics.pitfall: Including edges directed from T to S when summing cut capacity; only count edges directed from S to T.
topics.tip: Capacity of cut (S, T) = sum_{u in S, v in T} c(u, v).

topics.rule: A binary heap is a complete binary tree where all levels except possibly the last are fully filled from left to right.
topics.pitfall: Assuming heaps are fully sorted (left child is NOT guaranteed to be smaller/larger than right child).
topics.tip: Max-heap: root is absolute maximum. Min-heap: root is absolute minimum.

topics.rule: F[n] = F[n-1] + F[n-2] with F[0]=0, F[1]=1. Compute iteratively in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
topics.pitfall: Using 32-bit signed integer which overflows at F[47]. Use 64-bit integer (long long) for values up to F[92].
topics.tip: F[92] is the maximum Fibonacci number that fits into signed 64-bit integer.

topics.rule: Maintain recursive valid bounds (low, high). For left child, bound is (low, node.val); for right child, (node.val, high). Strictly low < key < high.
topics.pitfall: Checking only immediate children (left < root < right) fails when deep leaf violates an ancestor's bound.
topics.tip: Always check whole subtrees against ancestor bounds, not just parent-child pairs.

topics.rule: In-order traversal (Left -> Root -> Right) visits BST keys in monotonically ascending order. The k-th visited node is the k-th smallest element.
topics.pitfall: Confusing in-order with level-order or pre-order, or 0-indexed vs 1-indexed count.
topics.tip: Use iterative in-order traversal with a stack; stop as soon as k nodes are popped (O(H + k) time).

topics.rule: A Binary Search Tree requires every left descendant to be strictly less than the node, and every right descendant to be strictly greater.
topics.pitfall: Confusing a binary tree (at most 2 children per node) with a binary search tree (key ordering invariant).
topics.tip: Remember root has no parent, leaves have no children, and height is the max edges from root to leaf.

topics.rule: At current node: if key < curr.val go left, if key > curr.val go right. New nodes are always inserted as leaves.
topics.pitfall: Assuming standard BST automatically balances upon insertion; standard BST inserts without rotations.
topics.tip: Operations take O(H) time, which is O(log N) for balanced trees and O(N) for degenerate trees.

topics.rule: In-order traversal (Left -> Root -> Right) outputs keys of any BST in strictly increasing sorted order.
topics.pitfall: Mixing up in-order with pre-order (Root -> Left -> Right) or post-order (Left -> Right -> Root).
topics.tip: Whenever BST keys need to be flattened or verified as sorted, use in-order traversal.

topics.rule: Adjacency Matrix uses O(V^2) space and O(1) edge lookup. Adjacency List uses O(V + E) space and O(deg(v)) neighbor iteration.
topics.pitfall: Using Adjacency Matrix on sparse graphs with large V, causing O(V^2) memory exhaustion.
topics.tip: Always choose Adjacency List when E << V^2 to minimize memory and allow fast traversal.

topics.rule: A graph G = (V, E) connects vertices with edges. In undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional; handshaking lemma states sum(deg(v)) = 2E.
topics.pitfall: Assuming complete graph has V edges (a complete graph has V*(V-1)/2 edges).
topics.tip: Know edge counts: trees have V-1 edges, complete graphs have O(V^2) edges.

topics.rule: DFS explores deeply along each branch using recursion or a LIFO stack. Each traversal initiation from an unvisited vertex discovers a connected component.
topics.pitfall: Assuming DFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs (it finds any valid path, not the shortest).
topics.tip: To count components, loop over all vertices 1..V and trigger DFS whenever visited[i] is false.

topics.rule: Grows a single connected tree from an arbitrary starting vertex by always picking the cheapest crossing edge to an unvisited vertex using a min-heap.
topics.pitfall: Confusing Prim's single-tree growth with Kruskal's forest-merging approach.
topics.tip: Prim with min-heap runs in O((V + E) log V); best suited for dense graphs (E ~ V^2).

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.topic: Simulation via Priority Queue (Last Stone Weight)
topics.rule: Store stones in a max-heap. Repeatedly pop the two heaviest stones (y, x). If y > x, push y - x back into the heap.
topics.pitfall: Pushing 0 back into heap when y == x (both stones are completely smashed and nothing is pushed).
topics.tip: Simulate priority-based games by pairing a max-heap with loop termination when heap size <= 1.

topics.pitfall: Ignoring tie-breaking by row index (if soldier counts equal, smaller row index is weaker).
topics.tip: Binary search counts soldiers in each row in O(log C); heap keeps top k in O(R log k).

topics.rule: Sort greed factors and cookie sizes ascending. Greedily assign the smallest satisfying cookie to each child.
topics.pitfall: Giving an oversized cookie to a child with low greed, leaving large cookies unavailable for high-greed children.

topics.rule: Sort calories descending so that largest calories are multiplied by smallest powers of 2: sum(c[i] * 2^i).
topics.pitfall: Sorting in ascending order, causing largest calories to be multiplied by massive exponential factors.
topics.tip: When minimizing a weighted sum with increasing multipliers, pair largest items with smallest coefficients.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.
topics.pitfall: Applying greedy strategy to problems requiring exhaustive DP (e.g. 0/1 knapsack where value/weight greedy fails).
topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.rule: If s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]: dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: dp[i][j] = 0 (resets to 0 immediately on mismatch).
topics.pitfall: Propagating previous max values when characters do not match; substring must be contiguous.
topics.tip: Track global max length across all cells in the DP matrix.

topics.pitfall: Confusing subsequence (relative order preserved, non-contiguous) with substring (strictly contiguous characters).
topics.tip: LCS runs in O(M*N) time and can be optimized to O(min(M, N)) space using two rows.

topics.rule: Dynamic Programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure by memoizing subproblem results.
topics.pitfall: Using DP when subproblems do not overlap (divide-and-conquer is preferred then).
topics.tip: Ensure DP state representation captures all parameters needed to make subsequent transitions.

topics.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
topics.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.rule: Shortest path in unweighted 8-directional binary grid requires BFS. Mark cells visited upon pushing to queue.
topics.pitfall: Using DFS, which explores arbitrarily long paths and does not guarantee shortest distance.
topics.tip: First time queue reaches bottom-right cell (N-1, N-1) is the minimal path length.

topics.rule: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Base cases: start at step 0 or 1 with zero prior cost.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to take min of the final two steps to reach the top floor: min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).
topics.tip: Can be solved in O(1) auxiliary space using two variables prev1 and prev2.

topics.rule: All-pairs shortest path: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]). Intermediate vertex k loop MUST be outermost.
topics.pitfall: Placing intermediate vertex k loop inside the i, j loops, breaking DP intermediate-state invariants.
topics.tip: Runs in O(V^3) time. Finds city with smallest number of reachable neighbors within threshold.

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: Single-source shortest path on non-negative weighted graphs using min-heap. Time O((V + E) log V).
topics.pitfall: Running Dijkstra on graphs with negative edge weights (requires Bellman-Ford).
topics.tip: Network delay is max(dist[1..N]). If any node dist == inf, signal cannot reach all nodes (return -1).

topics.rule: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1]; else 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).
topics.pitfall: Adding cost +1 when characters match; matching characters cost 0 edits.
topics.tip: Base cases: dp[i][0] = i (deleting i chars), dp[0][j] = j (inserting j chars).

topics.rule: m[i][j] = min_{i<=k<j} (m[i][k] + m[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j]). Base case m[i][i] = 0.
topics.pitfall: Multiplying matrices directly instead of finding the optimal split point k that minimizes scalar multiplications.
topics.tip: Compute by chain length L = 2 to n. Optimal parenthesization drastically reduces arithmetic ops.

topics.topic: Minimum s-t Cut Principle & Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
topics.rule: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem: Maximum flow through network equals minimum capacity among all cuts separating source s and sink t.
topics.pitfall: Including edges directed from T to S when summing cut capacity; only count edges directed from S to T.
topics.tip: Capacity of cut (S, T) = sum_{u in S, v in T} c(u, v).

topics.rule: Sort calories descending so that largest calories are multiplied by smallest powers of 2: sum(c[i] * 2^i).
topics.pitfall: Sorting in ascending order, causing largest calories to be multiplied by massive exponential factors.
topics.tip: When minimizing a weighted sum with increasing multipliers, pair largest items with smallest coefficients.

topics.rule: Sort box types descending by units per box. Greedily pack as many boxes of highest unit count as possible.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by number of boxes rather than unit capacity per box.
topics.tip: Greedy choice by unit density is optimal here because box types are divisible up to box units.

topics.rule: Flow conservation: sum of flow into any node u (except s and t) must equal sum of flow out. Capacity constraint: 0 <= f(e) <= c(e).
topics.pitfall: Assuming flow conservation applies to source s or sink t; net flow leaves s and enters t.
topics.tip: Total flow value equals net flow out of source s.

topics.rule: m[i][j] = min_{i<=k<j} (m[i][k] + m[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j]). Base case m[i][i] = 0.
topics.pitfall: Multiplying matrices directly instead of finding the optimal split point k that minimizes scalar multiplications.
topics.tip: Compute by chain length L = 2 to n. Optimal parenthesization drastically reduces arithmetic ops.

topics.rule: Sort all edges by weight in ascending order. Add edge (u, v) iff find(u) != find(v) (prevents cycles). Stop at V - 1 edges.
topics.pitfall: Adding an edge between vertices already in the same component, creating a cycle and violating tree property.
topics.tip: DSU with path compression and union-by-rank guarantees nearly linear O(E alpha(V)) runtime.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.rule: Dynamic Programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure by memoizing subproblem results.
topics.pitfall: Using DP when subproblems do not overlap (divide-and-conquer is preferred then).
topics.tip: Ensure DP state representation captures all parameters needed to make subsequent transitions.

topics.rule: F[n] = F[n-1] + F[n-2] with F[0]=0, F[1]=1. Compute iteratively in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
topics.pitfall: Using 32-bit signed integer which overflows at F[47]. Use 64-bit integer (long long) for values up to F[92].
topics.tip: F[92] is the maximum Fibonacci number that fits into signed 64-bit integer.

topics.rule: Forward residual capacity c_f(u, v) = c(u, v) - f(u, v). Backward residual capacity c_f(v, u) = f(u, v) enables flow cancellation.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to add backward edge with capacity equal to sent flow, preventing cancellation of suboptimal earlier decisions.
topics.tip: Residual network allows searching for augmentations even after initial flows are pushed.

topics.rule: When giving change for $20, prioritize giving one $10 and one $5 bill over three $5 bills.
topics.pitfall: Consuming three $5 bills for $20 change when a $10 bill is available, leaving no $5 bills for subsequent $10 customers.
topics.tip: $5 bills are required for both $10 and $20 customers, so preserve them greedily.

topics.rule: Sort greed factors and cookie sizes ascending. Greedily assign the smallest satisfying cookie to each child.
topics.pitfall: Giving an oversized cookie to a child with low greed, leaving large cookies unavailable for high-greed children.
topics.tip: Sorting both arrays allows single-pass two-pointer linear match in O(N log N + M log M).

topics.rule: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Base cases: start at step 0 or 1 with zero prior cost.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to take min of the final two steps to reach the top floor: min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).
topics.tip: Can be solved in O(1) auxiliary space using two variables prev1 and prev2.

topics.rule: A graph G = (V, E) connects vertices with edges. In undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional; handshaking lemma states sum(deg(v)) = 2E.
topics.pitfall: Assuming complete graph has V edges (a complete graph has V*(V-1)/2 edges).
topics.tip: Know edge counts: trees have V-1 edges, complete graphs have O(V^2) edges.

topics.rule: BFS explores vertices level-by-level using a FIFO Queue. In unweighted graphs, BFS guarantees finding shortest paths in fewest edges.
topics.pitfall: Failing to mark vertices visited upon enqueue, resulting in redundant processing and memory explosion.
topics.tip: BFS time complexity is O(V + E). Perfect for maze routing and unweighted reachability.

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.
topics.pitfall: Applying greedy strategy to problems requiring exhaustive DP (e.g. 0/1 knapsack where value/weight greedy fails).
topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
topics.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.rule: Minimum endpoint deletions to make two strings identical equals (len(s1) + len(s2) - 2 * LCS(s1, s2)).
topics.pitfall: Trying arbitrary character removals without recognizing that preserved characters form the LCS.
topics.tip: Reducing string edit problems to LCS often yields straightforward DP solutions.

topics.pitfall: Confusing subsequence (relative order preserved, non-contiguous) with substring (strictly contiguous characters).
topics.tip: LCS runs in O(M*N) time and can be optimized to O(min(M, N)) space using two rows.

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: Sort both arrays. Two-pointer matching satisfies the maximum number of children.
topics.pitfall: Failing to sort both greed and size arrays prior to matching.
topics.tip: Pair smallest satisfactory resource to each demand.

topics.rule: All-pairs shortest path: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]). Intermediate vertex k loop MUST be outermost.
topics.pitfall: Placing intermediate vertex k loop inside the i, j loops, breaking DP intermediate-state invariants.
topics.tip: Runs in O(V^3) time. Finds city with smallest number of reachable neighbors within threshold.

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.topic: Merge K Sorted Lists via Min-Heap

topics.pitfall: Inserting all N total elements into the heap at once (takes O(N log N) space/time instead of O(N log k)).
topics.tip: Heap size never exceeds k, yielding optimal O(N log k) time complexity.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.

topics.tip: Prim with min-heap runs in O((V + E) log V); best suited for dense graphs (E ~ V^2).

topics.rule: Sort all edges by weight in ascending order. Add edge (u, v) iff find(u) != find(v) (prevents cycles). Stop at V - 1 edges.
topics.pitfall: Adding an edge between vertices already in the same component, creating a cycle and violating tree property.
topics.tip: DSU with path compression and union-by-rank guarantees nearly linear O(E alpha(V)) runtime.

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.
topics.pitfall: Applying greedy strategy to problems requiring exhaustive DP (e.g. 0/1 knapsack where value/weight greedy fails).
topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: Sort both arrays. Two-pointer matching satisfies the maximum number of children.
topics.pitfall: Failing to sort both greed and size arrays prior to matching.
topics.tip: Pair smallest satisfactory resource to each demand.

topics.rule: F[n] = F[n-1] + F[n-2] with F[0]=0, F[1]=1. Compute iteratively in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
topics.pitfall: Using 32-bit signed integer which overflows at F[47]. Use 64-bit integer (long long) for values up to F[92].
topics.tip: F[92] is the maximum Fibonacci number that fits into signed 64-bit integer.

topics.pitfall: Confusing subsequence (relative order preserved, non-contiguous) with substring (strictly contiguous characters).
topics.tip: LCS runs in O(M*N) time and can be optimized to O(min(M, N)) space using two rows.

topics.rule: Forward residual capacity c_f(u, v) = c(u, v) - f(u, v). Backward residual capacity c_f(v, u) = f(u, v) enables flow cancellation.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to add backward edge with capacity equal to sent flow, preventing cancellation of suboptimal earlier decisions.
topics.tip: Residual network allows searching for augmentations even after initial flows are pushed.

topics.rule: In-order traversal (Left -> Root -> Right) outputs keys of any BST in strictly increasing sorted order.
topics.pitfall: Mixing up in-order with pre-order (Root -> Left -> Right) or post-order (Left -> Right -> Root).
topics.tip: Whenever BST keys need to be flattened or verified as sorted, use in-order traversal.

topics.rule: At current node: if key < curr.val go left, if key > curr.val go right. New nodes are always inserted as leaves.
topics.pitfall: Assuming standard BST automatically balances upon insertion; standard BST inserts without rotations.
topics.tip: Operations take O(H) time, which is O(log N) for balanced trees and O(N) for degenerate trees.

topics.rule: Maintain recursive valid bounds (low, high). For left child, bound is (low, node.val); for right child, (node.val, high). Strictly low < key < high.
topics.pitfall: Checking only immediate children (left < root < right) fails when deep leaf violates an ancestor's bound.
topics.tip: Always check whole subtrees against ancestor bounds, not just parent-child pairs.

topics.rule: In-order traversal (Left -> Root -> Right) visits BST keys in monotonically ascending order. The k-th visited node is the k-th smallest element.
topics.pitfall: Confusing in-order with level-order or pre-order, or 0-indexed vs 1-indexed count.
topics.tip: Use iterative in-order traversal with a stack; stop as soon as k nodes are popped (O(H + k) time).

topics.rule: A Binary Search Tree requires every left descendant to be strictly less than the node, and every right descendant to be strictly greater.
topics.pitfall: Confusing a binary tree (at most 2 children per node) with a binary search tree (key ordering invariant).
topics.tip: Remember root has no parent, leaves have no children, and height is the max edges from root to leaf.

topics.rule: DFS explores deeply along each branch using recursion or a LIFO stack. Each traversal initiation from an unvisited vertex discovers a connected component.
topics.pitfall: Assuming DFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs (it finds any valid path, not the shortest).
topics.tip: To count components, loop over all vertices 1..V and trigger DFS whenever visited[i] is false.

topics.rule: A graph G = (V, E) connects vertices with edges. In undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional; handshaking lemma states sum(deg(v)) = 2E.
topics.pitfall: Assuming complete graph has V edges (a complete graph has V*(V-1)/2 edges).
topics.tip: Know edge counts: trees have V-1 edges, complete graphs have O(V^2) edges.

topics.rule: Adjacency Matrix uses O(V^2) space and O(1) edge lookup. Adjacency List uses O(V + E) space and O(deg(v)) neighbor iteration.
topics.pitfall: Using Adjacency Matrix on sparse graphs with large V, causing O(V^2) memory exhaustion.
topics.tip: Always choose Adjacency List when E << V^2 to minimize memory and allow fast traversal.

topics.rule: Cut Property: For any partition of V into (S, V - S), the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to some MST. If weights are distinct, MST is unique.
topics.pitfall: Confusing MST (minimizes sum of all edge weights) with shortest path tree (minimizes distance from a single source).
topics.tip: A spanning tree on V vertices always contains exactly V - 1 edges and no cycles.

topics.rule: BFS explores vertices level-by-level using a FIFO Queue. In unweighted graphs, BFS guarantees finding shortest paths in fewest edges.
topics.pitfall: Failing to mark vertices visited upon enqueue, resulting in redundant processing and memory explosion.
topics.tip: BFS time complexity is O(V + E). Perfect for maze routing and unweighted reachability.

topics.rule: Sort boxes descending by units per box. Greedily take as many boxes of highest unit density as truck capacity allows.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by box count rather than units per box.
topics.tip: Fractional greedy knapsack property guarantees optimal total units.

topics.rule: Sort athletes by score descending. Assign 'Gold Medal', 'Silver Medal', 'Bronze Medal' to top 3, and numeric ranks '4', '5' onwards.
topics.pitfall: Zero-indexing the string ranks or scrambling the original array positions.
topics.tip: Store index pairs (score, original_index) in a max-heap to write results directly to output array.

topics.topic: Merge K Sorted Lists via Min-Heap
topics.rule: Insert head node of each of the k lists into a min-heap. Pop smallest, append to merged list, and push next node from that list.
topics.pitfall: Inserting all N total elements into the heap at once (takes O(N log N) space/time instead of O(N log k)).
topics.tip: Heap size never exceeds k, yielding optimal O(N log k) time complexity.

topics.rule: Sort the array in O(N log N). The minimum difference between any two elements is guaranteed to occur between adjacent elements.
topics.pitfall: Comparing all pairs in O(N^2) time or comparing only maximum and minimum.
topics.tip: Sort first, then do a single linear scan checking A[i+1] - A[i].

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
topics.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.rule: Sort box types descending by units per box. Greedily pack as many boxes of highest unit count as possible.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by number of boxes rather than unit capacity per box.
topics.tip: Greedy choice by unit density is optimal here because box types are divisible up to box units.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.rule: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Base cases: start at step 0 or 1 with zero prior cost.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to take min of the final two steps to reach the top floor: min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]).
topics.tip: Can be solved in O(1) auxiliary space using two variables prev1 and prev2.

topics.rule: Single-source shortest path on non-negative weighted graphs using min-heap. Time O((V + E) log V).
topics.pitfall: Running Dijkstra on graphs with negative edge weights (requires Bellman-Ford).
topics.tip: Network delay is max(dist[1..N]). If any node dist == inf, signal cannot reach all nodes (return -1).

topics.rule: Traverse 4 directions. If neighbor equals initial color, change to target color and recurse.
topics.pitfall: Infinite recursion if initial color equals target color; check and return immediately.
topics.tip: Always check grid boundaries 0 <= r < R and 0 <= c < C before accessing cells.

topics.topic: Minimum s-t Cut Principle & Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
topics.rule: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem: Maximum flow through network equals minimum capacity among all cuts separating source s and sink t.
topics.pitfall: Including edges directed from T to S when summing cut capacity; only count edges directed from S to T.
topics.tip: Capacity of cut (S, T) = sum_{u in S, v in T} c(u, v).

topics.rule: Sort all edges by weight in ascending order. Add edge (u, v) iff find(u) != find(v) (prevents cycles). Stop at V - 1 edges.

topics.rule: Cut Property: For any partition of V into (S, V - S), the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to some MST. If weights are distinct, MST is unique.
topics.pitfall: Confusing MST (minimizes sum of all edge weights) with shortest path tree (minimizes distance from a single source).
topics.tip: A spanning tree on V vertices always contains exactly V - 1 edges and no cycles.

topics.rule: BFS explores vertices level-by-level using a FIFO Queue. In unweighted graphs, BFS guarantees finding shortest paths in fewest edges.

topics.rule: Insert: append to end and bubble up (O(log N)). Extract: replace root with last element and sift down (O(log N)). Build-heap: bottom-up heapify in O(N).
topics.pitfall: Thinking build-heap takes O(N log N); mathematical summation shows bottom-up heapify takes strictly O(N) linear time.
topics.tip: Parent is at (i - 1) // 2; children are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 for 0-indexed arrays.

topics.rule: Sort athletes by score descending. Assign 'Gold Medal', 'Silver Medal', 'Bronze Medal' to top 3, and numeric ranks '4', '5' onwards.

topics.tip: Store index pairs (score, original_index) in a max-heap to write results directly to output array.

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.

topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: Sort calories descending so that largest calories are multiplied by smallest powers of 2: sum(c[i] * 2^i).
topics.pitfall: Sorting in ascending order, causing largest calories to be multiplied by massive exponential factors.
topics.tip: When minimizing a weighted sum with increasing multipliers, pair largest items with smallest coefficients.

topics.rule: Sort greed factors and cookie sizes ascending. Greedily assign the smallest satisfying cookie to each child.
topics.pitfall: Giving an oversized cookie to a child with low greed, leaving large cookies unavailable for high-greed children.
topics.tip: Sorting both arrays allows single-pass two-pointer linear match in O(N log N + M log M).

topics.rule: When giving change for $20, prioritize giving one $10 and one $5 bill over three $5 bills.
topics.pitfall: Consuming three $5 bills for $20 change when a $10 bill is available, leaving no $5 bills for subsequent $10 customers.
topics.tip: $5 bills are required for both $10 and $20 customers, so preserve them greedily.

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.rule: Dynamic Programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure by memoizing subproblem results.
topics.pitfall: Using DP when subproblems do not overlap (divide-and-conquer is preferred then).
topics.tip: Ensure DP state representation captures all parameters needed to make subsequent transitions.

topics.rule: Sort box types descending by units per box. Greedily pack as many boxes of highest unit count as possible.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by number of boxes rather than unit capacity per box.
topics.tip: Greedy choice by unit density is optimal here because box types are divisible up to box units.

topics.rule: Sort both arrays. Two-pointer matching satisfies the maximum number of children.
topics.pitfall: Failing to sort both greed and size arrays prior to matching.
topics.tip: Pair smallest satisfactory resource to each demand.

topics.rule: Single-source shortest path on non-negative weighted graphs using min-heap. Time O((V + E) log V).
topics.pitfall: Running Dijkstra on graphs with negative edge weights (requires Bellman-Ford).

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.tip: First time queue reaches bottom-right cell (N-1, N-1) is the minimal path length.

topics.rule: Flow conservation: sum of flow into any node u (except s and t) must equal sum of flow out. Capacity constraint: 0 <= f(e) <= c(e).
topics.pitfall: Assuming flow conservation applies to source s or sink t; net flow leaves s and enters t.
topics.tip: Total flow value equals net flow out of source s.

topics.pitfall: Sorting in ascending order, causing largest calories to be multiplied by massive exponential factors.
topics.tip: When minimizing a weighted sum with increasing multipliers, pair largest items with smallest coefficients.

topics.rule: Sort flower prices descending. Buy most expensive flowers in the earliest round (multiplier 1), distributing purchases round-robin.
topics.pitfall: Letting one person buy multiple flowers while another has bought none, needlessly increasing the price multiplier.
topics.tip: Round-robin distribution minimizes maximum purchase multiplier across k friends.

topics.rule: Flow conservation: sum of flow into any node u (except s and t) must equal sum of flow out. Capacity constraint: 0 <= f(e) <= c(e).
topics.pitfall: Assuming flow conservation applies to source s or sink t; net flow leaves s and enters t.
topics.tip: Total flow value equals net flow out of source s.

topics.rule: Forward residual capacity c_f(u, v) = c(u, v) - f(u, v). Backward residual capacity c_f(v, u) = f(u, v) enables flow cancellation.
topics.pitfall: Forgetting to add backward edge with capacity equal to sent flow, preventing cancellation of suboptimal earlier decisions.
topics.tip: Residual network allows searching for augmentations even after initial flows are pushed.

topics.rule: m[i][j] = min_{i<=k<j} (m[i][k] + m[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j]). Base case m[i][i] = 0.
topics.pitfall: Multiplying matrices directly instead of finding the optimal split point k that minimizes scalar multiplications.
topics.tip: Compute by chain length L = 2 to n. Optimal parenthesization drastically reduces arithmetic ops.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.rule: A binary heap is a complete binary tree where all levels except possibly the last are fully filled from left to right.
topics.pitfall: Assuming heaps are fully sorted (left child is NOT guaranteed to be smaller/larger than right child).
topics.tip: Max-heap: root is absolute maximum. Min-heap: root is absolute minimum.

topics.rule: F[n] = F[n-1] + F[n-2] with F[0]=0, F[1]=1. Compute iteratively in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
topics.pitfall: Using 32-bit signed integer which overflows at F[47]. Use 64-bit integer (long long) for values up to F[92].
topics.tip: F[92] is the maximum Fibonacci number that fits into signed 64-bit integer.

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.
topics.pitfall: Applying greedy strategy to problems requiring exhaustive DP (e.g. 0/1 knapsack where value/weight greedy fails).
topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: When giving change for $20, prioritize giving one $10 and one $5 bill over three $5 bills.
topics.pitfall: Consuming three $5 bills for $20 change when a $10 bill is available, leaving no $5 bills for subsequent $10 customers.
topics.tip: $5 bills are required for both $10 and $20 customers, so preserve them greedily.

topics.rule: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1]; else 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).
topics.pitfall: Adding cost +1 when characters match; matching characters cost 0 edits.
topics.tip: Base cases: dp[i][0] = i (deleting i chars), dp[0][j] = j (inserting j chars).

topics.rule: Sort boxes descending by units per box. Greedily take as many boxes of highest unit density as truck capacity allows.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by box count rather than units per box.
topics.tip: Fractional greedy knapsack property guarantees optimal total units.

topics.topic: K Weakest Rows using Priority Queue
topics.rule: Score each row by soldier count. Use a max-heap of size k with comparator (soldier_count, row_index) to retain k weakest rows.
topics.pitfall: Ignoring tie-breaking by row index (if soldier counts equal, smaller row index is weaker).
topics.tip: Binary search counts soldiers in each row in O(log C); heap keeps top k in O(R log k).

topics.rule: Sort athletes by score descending. Assign 'Gold Medal', 'Silver Medal', 'Bronze Medal' to top 3, and numeric ranks '4', '5' onwards.
topics.pitfall: Zero-indexing the string ranks or scrambling the original array positions.
topics.tip: Store index pairs (score, original_index) in a max-heap to write results directly to output array.

topics.topic: Simulation via Priority Queue (Last Stone Weight)
topics.rule: Store stones in a max-heap. Repeatedly pop the two heaviest stones (y, x). If y > x, push y - x back into the heap.
topics.pitfall: Pushing 0 back into heap when y == x (both stones are completely smashed and nothing is pushed).
topics.tip: Simulate priority-based games by pairing a max-heap with loop termination when heap size <= 1.

topics.rule: Count element frequencies with a hash map. Push (frequency, element) pairs into a min-heap of size k. Heap retains k most frequent.
topics.pitfall: Sorting elements by value instead of frequency in the priority queue.
topics.tip: Min-heap of size k yields O(N log k) time. Bucket sort can solve it in O(N).

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.rule: Sort the array in O(N log N). The minimum difference between any two elements is guaranteed to occur between adjacent elements.
topics.pitfall: Comparing all pairs in O(N^2) time or comparing only maximum and minimum.
topics.tip: Sort first, then do a single linear scan checking A[i+1] - A[i].

topics.rule: Sort box types descending by units per box. Greedily pack as many boxes of highest unit count as possible.
topics.pitfall: Sorting by number of boxes rather than unit capacity per box.
topics.tip: Greedy choice by unit density is optimal here because box types are divisible up to box units.

topics.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
topics.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.pitfall: Confusing subsequence (relative order preserved, non-contiguous) with substring (strictly contiguous characters).
topics.tip: LCS runs in O(M*N) time and can be optimized to O(min(M, N)) space using two rows.

topics.rule: Minimum endpoint deletions to make two strings identical equals (len(s1) + len(s2) - 2 * LCS(s1, s2)).
topics.pitfall: Trying arbitrary character removals without recognizing that preserved characters form the LCS.
topics.tip: Reducing string edit problems to LCS often yields straightforward DP solutions.

topics.rule: If s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]: dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: dp[i][j] = 0 (resets to 0 immediately on mismatch).
topics.pitfall: Propagating previous max values when characters do not match; substring must be contiguous.
topics.tip: Track global max length across all cells in the DP matrix.

topics.rule: Single-source shortest path on non-negative weighted graphs using min-heap. Time O((V + E) log V).
topics.pitfall: Running Dijkstra on graphs with negative edge weights (requires Bellman-Ford).
topics.tip: Network delay is max(dist[1..N]). If any node dist == inf, signal cannot reach all nodes (return -1).

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: All-pairs shortest path: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]). Intermediate vertex k loop MUST be outermost.
topics.pitfall: Placing intermediate vertex k loop inside the i, j loops, breaking DP intermediate-state invariants.
topics.tip: Runs in O(V^3) time. Finds city with smallest number of reachable neighbors within threshold.

topics.pitfall: Assuming heaps are fully sorted (left child is NOT guaranteed to be smaller/larger than right child).

topics.rule: Cut Property: For any partition of V into (S, V - S), the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to some MST. If weights are distinct, MST is unique.
topics.pitfall: Confusing MST (minimizes sum of all edge weights) with shortest path tree (minimizes distance from a single source).
topics.tip: A spanning tree on V vertices always contains exactly V - 1 edges and no cycles.

topics.rule: DFS explores deeply along each branch using recursion or a LIFO stack. Each traversal initiation from an unvisited vertex discovers a connected component.
topics.pitfall: Assuming DFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs (it finds any valid path, not the shortest).
topics.tip: To count components, loop over all vertices 1..V and trigger DFS whenever visited[i] is false.

topics.rule: A graph G = (V, E) connects vertices with edges. In undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional; handshaking lemma states sum(deg(v)) = 2E.
topics.pitfall: Assuming complete graph has V edges (a complete graph has V*(V-1)/2 edges).
topics.tip: Know edge counts: trees have V-1 edges, complete graphs have O(V^2) edges.

topics.rule: Count element frequencies with a hash map. Push (frequency, element) pairs into a min-heap of size k. Heap retains k most frequent.
topics.pitfall: Sorting elements by value instead of frequency in the priority queue.
topics.tip: Min-heap of size k yields O(N log k) time. Bucket sort can solve it in O(N).

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.rule: Sort greed factors and cookie sizes ascending. Greedily assign the smallest satisfying cookie to each child.
topics.pitfall: Giving an oversized cookie to a child with low greed, leaving large cookies unavailable for high-greed children.
topics.tip: Sorting both arrays allows single-pass two-pointer linear match in O(N log N + M log M).

topics.rule: Sort the array in O(N log N). The minimum difference between any two elements is guaranteed to occur between adjacent elements.
topics.pitfall: Comparing all pairs in O(N^2) time or comparing only maximum and minimum.
topics.tip: Sort first, then do a single linear scan checking A[i+1] - A[i].

topics.rule: Track max_reach = max(max_reach, i + nums[i]). If at any index i > max_reach, the end is unreachable (return false).
topics.pitfall: Using backtracking or full DP table O(N^2) when greedy reachability runs in O(N) time and O(1) space.
topics.tip: If max_reach >= last_index at any point, immediately return true.

topics.rule: Dynamic Programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure by memoizing subproblem results.
topics.pitfall: Using DP when subproblems do not overlap (divide-and-conquer is preferred then).
topics.tip: Ensure DP state representation captures all parameters needed to make subsequent transitions.

topics.rule: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - wt[i]] + val[i]). In 1D space, iterate w backwards from W down to wt[i].
topics.pitfall: Iterating capacity forwards in 1D array, which allows the same item to be reused multiple times (unbounded knapsack).
topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.rule: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1]; else 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).
topics.pitfall: Adding cost +1 when characters match; matching characters cost 0 edits.
topics.tip: Base cases: dp[i][0] = i (deleting i chars), dp[0][j] = j (inserting j chars).

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.
topics.pitfall: Taking highest absolute value instead of highest value density.
topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: Score each row by soldier count. Use a max-heap of size k with comparator (soldier_count, row_index) to retain k weakest rows.
topics.pitfall: Ignoring tie-breaking by row index (if soldier counts equal, smaller row index is weaker).
topics.tip: Binary search counts soldiers in each row in O(log C); heap keeps top k in O(R log k).

topics.rule: A binary heap is a complete binary tree where all levels except possibly the last are fully filled from left to right.

topics.rule: Count element frequencies with a hash map. Push (frequency, element) pairs into a min-heap of size k. Heap retains k most frequent.
topics.pitfall: Sorting elements by value instead of frequency in the priority queue.
topics.tip: Min-heap of size k yields O(N log k) time. Bucket sort can solve it in O(N).

topics.rule: Insert: append to end and bubble up (O(log N)). Extract: replace root with last element and sift down (O(log N)). Build-heap: bottom-up heapify in O(N).
topics.pitfall: Thinking build-heap takes O(N log N); mathematical summation shows bottom-up heapify takes strictly O(N) linear time.
topics.tip: Parent is at (i - 1) // 2; children are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 for 0-indexed arrays.

topics.rule: Maintain a Min-Heap of size k. For each new item, push and pop smallest if heap size > k. The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element.
topics.pitfall: Using a max-heap of size N (O(N) space) instead of a size-k min-heap (O(k) space, O(N log k) time).
topics.tip: To find K-th largest, use a MIN-heap of size k. To find K-th smallest, use a MAX-heap of size k.

topics.rule: When giving change for $20, prioritize giving one $10 and one $5 bill over three $5 bills.
topics.pitfall: Consuming three $5 bills for $20 change when a $10 bill is available, leaving no $5 bills for subsequent $10 customers.
topics.tip: $5 bills are required for both $10 and $20 customers, so preserve them greedily.

topics.rule: Sort greed factors and cookie sizes ascending. Greedily assign the smallest satisfying cookie to each child.
topics.pitfall: Giving an oversized cookie to a child with low greed, leaving large cookies unavailable for high-greed children.
topics.tip: Sorting both arrays allows single-pass two-pointer linear match in O(N log N + M log M).

topics.rule: Greedy choice property: a locally optimal choice leads to a global optimum without backtracking. Requires optimal substructure.
topics.pitfall: Applying greedy strategy to problems requiring exhaustive DP (e.g. 0/1 knapsack where value/weight greedy fails).
topics.tip: Always formulate an exchange argument or check for counterexamples to prove greedy correctness.

topics.rule: Dynamic Programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure by memoizing subproblem results.
topics.pitfall: Using DP when subproblems do not overlap (divide-and-conquer is preferred then).
topics.tip: Ensure DP state representation captures all parameters needed to make subsequent transitions.

topics.rule: If total_sum % 2 != 0, return false immediately. Else target = total_sum / 2; solve boolean subset sum DP.
topics.pitfall: Attempting to partition an odd total sum, which is mathematically impossible for integers.
topics.tip: Boolean array dp[w] updated backwards from target down to num: dp[w] = dp[w] or dp[w - num].

topics.tip: Backward iteration ensures each item is used at most once in 0/1 knapsack.

topics.pitfall: Failing to sort both greed and size arrays prior to matching.

topics.rule: Sort items descending by efficiency ratio (value / weight). Greedily allocate items of highest ratio until target value is met.

topics.tip: Inverse fractional knapsack minimizes total weight needed to reach target value.

topics.rule: A binary heap is a complete binary tree where all levels except possibly the last are fully filled from left to right.
topics.pitfall: Assuming heaps are fully sorted (left child is NOT guaranteed to be smaller/larger than right child).
topics.tip: Max-heap: root is absolute maximum. Min-heap: root is absolute minimum.
